caption: The drawing is composed of two detailed black-and-white line illustrations of oval-shaped objects, both suspended from what appears to be a tied cloth or ribbon. The object on the left is labeled "OBVERSE," and the object on the right is labeled "REVERSE." Both objects have intricate designs and inscriptions inside the oval frame. The obverse features a central area with the text "TO THE MEMORY OF MRS. DICKASON, She Died Dec. 25th, 1802 Aged 40," accompanied by an illustration of an urn on a pedestal with floral decorations beneath the text, and a scene above with what appears to be a cherub or angel reclining. The reverse shows a similar oval object, also with an urn at the bottom center, and above it, an inscription with smaller, more densely-packed writing, as well as the phrase "MEMENTO MORI" and the word "Denial" towards the top. Both objects are vertically oriented and centrally placed on an off-white or cream-colored background with ample blank space around them. The name "LAWRENCE FLYNN" appears in small print in the lower-right corner of the page.
title: Silver Momento
